The Bardiche is built around a VOX 330 XL fusion plant that pushes its 70-ton frame to a maximum speed of 86 kilometers per hour. Its Alice Z-20 transmission provides full flank speed in reverse, a feature that gives the vehicle its most meaningful tactical advantage by allowing it to disengage without turning its rear to the enemy. The armament suite is broad but inconsistent: an Octagon Siren iNarc Missile Beacon handles target designation, a Holly 7-Tube Multi-Missile Launcher provides flexible fire support, two Fusigon Shorttooth Light Particle Projection Cannons address close-range threats, four Corean Magshot Gauss Rifles deliver sustained anti-infantry suppression, and two Earthwerks Model 4 Mine Dispensers offer battlefield denial capability. Riese 400 Reactive armor provides reasonable protection against conventional munitions.

The vehicle's core weakness is its sprawling, unfocused weapons load, which renders it poorly suited to direct engagement against any specific threat class. A 3121 service bulletin restricting deployment to breathable-atmosphere environments further limits its operational flexibility. Multiple field-serviceable upgrade packages have been issued over the years without meaningfully resolving these fundamental deficiencies.

The Bardiche Heavy Strike Tank was developed by Earthwerks-FWL, Incorporated for the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth in the early Dark Age, entering production in 3101. Originally conceived as an infantry support platform to serve alongside BattleMech forces, the Bardiche was intended to leverage its wheeled chassis for high-speed repositioning while delivering sustained fire against lighter opposing units. Despite its ambitious design goals, the vehicle quickly developed a troubled reputation, with critics famously describing it as little more than an expensive liability in the field. Earthwerks marketed the Bardiche aggressively through a series of incentivized deals and broad procurement arrangements, making it a surprisingly common sight in militias and second-line regiments across Free Worlds League space. Its reputation has never fully recovered from its difficult early service record, though it continues to serve in significant numbers wherever Earthwerks-FWL maintains manufacturing influence.

The C variant was developed under Clan Wolf Empire oversight following the conquest of Keystone, entering production in 3143. Engineered to Clan standards, it represents an effort to extract continued military utility from the captured Earthwerks-FWL production line without committing scarce Clan OmniMech resources to routine defensive assignments. The variant is concentrated in Clan Wolf Empire territory and has seen limited distribution beyond that faction's holdings. Its combat record under Clan Wolf Empire colors remains modest, consistent with the Bardiche's established limitations as a general-purpose combat vehicle.

The Bardiche entered production at Earthwerks-FWL's Keystone facility in 3101, developed to meet a Marik-Stewart Commonwealth requirement for an affordable heavy infantry support platform. Despite early procurement enthusiasm, the design's tactical limitations became apparent almost immediately, and the vehicle earned persistent criticism for its poor handling of hostile environments and its failure to perform effectively in the support roles it was designed for. The Minesweeper variant followed in 3114, addressing one narrow operational gap by sacrificing direct-fire capability for dedicated mine-clearance equipment.

Production expanded to the Calloway VI facility as Earthwerks-FWL worked to meet continued MSC demand, though neither plant resolved the shortcomings that defined the Bardiche's service history. During the Dark Age, Keystone became a focal point of Clan Wolf aggression when two Supernova Binaries were dispatched to seize the planet's manufacturing infrastructure. Bardiche crews assigned to the defense played a decisive role in protecting the Breckwind Combat Vehicle Plant, establishing minefields along the mountain approaches and drawing the Wolf advance into prepared killing grounds. The Breckwind facility ultimately held, becoming the only Earthwerks-FWL location to repulse the Clan Wolf assault, and earning its senior defender a Defensive Operations Ribbon for the engagement. The rest of Keystone fell to the Wolves, transferring production of subsequent variants to Clan Wolf Empire oversight. The Calloway VI line continued under successive Marik successor states and eventually returned to Free Worlds League control, remaining active into the ilClan era.

The Anhur's fusion powerplant drives it to flanking speeds that make it one of the faster cargo VTOLs in service, and its tilt-rotor design enables takeoff and landing on unprepared surfaces without the need for prepared runways. The seven-ton cargo bay accommodates bulk supplies or a full infantry squad, with internal tie-down points supporting a wide variety of load configurations. A crew of pilot, copilot, and loadmaster specializes in low-altitude, terrain-following flight profiles that keep the vehicle below typical threat acquisition systems.

For self-defense, the Anhur carries a forward-facing extended-range medium laser alongside a medium pulse laser in the chin mount, providing both range and rapid-fire capability against light opponents and infantry. A second medium pulse laser covers the rear arc, deterring pursuit after cargo deliveries. Three tons of ferro-fibrous armor gives the design more protection than most VTOLs carry, though the Anhur's primary defensive strategy remains speed and terrain masking rather than absorbing punishment. This armament can suppress light threats and clear contested landing zones, but the design is not intended to engage BattleMechs or heavy armor.

The Anhur Transport is a Clan logistics vehicle developed around 2840 from the Star League Defense Force's Cobra Transport VTOL, examples of which traveled with the SLDF during the Exodus into the Deep Periphery. Intended to address the practical limitations of using DropShips for planetside supply runs, the Anhur fills the role of surface-level logistics transport, moving materiel from landing zones to forward units across terrain that larger craft cannot efficiently service. Produced across multiple Clan homeworld facilities rather than a single dedicated manufacturer, the design serves in the toumans of virtually every Clan as the standard means of bridging the gap between orbital delivery and the forward edge of the battle area.

This unique conversion was operated by a Dark Caste raider band in the Clan Homeworlds region, documented during raids on Ghost Bear installations on Constance in 3074. Its long-range missiles and Inner Sphere stealth systems allow the craft to stand off at range while remaining difficult to detect, making it well suited to harassment operations against supply convoys and garrison stations. Ghost Bear forces found their standard detection systems frustrated by its stealth suite, though ground-based hovertank patrols ultimately forced the band's withdrawal from the Constance system.

The Anhur's lineage runs to the Star League Defense Force's Cobra Transport VTOL, a logistics design that entered service in 2582 during the Reunification War and proved so successful that it became standard equipment across SLDF formations. When General Aleksandr Kerensky led the SLDF on its Exodus in 2784, Cobra transports traveled with the fleet into the Deep Periphery, where the emerging Clans retained them as part of their inherited logistical base.

As the Clans reorganized and rebuilt their military infrastructure over the following generations, their engineers adapted the aging Cobra design to Clan technical standards, producing the Anhur around 2840. The name draws from ancient Terran mythology, referencing a deity of war and the hunt, consistent with Clan naming traditions. Unlike many Clan weapons that see continual revision, the Anhur underwent relatively little modification from its initial form, a reflection of the soundness of the original Cobra platform. Production was established across multiple Clan homeworld facilities, with individual Clans operating their own manufacturing lines on planets including Albion, Babylon, Lum, Niles, Roche, Shadow, and York.

The distribution of Anhur production across multiple Clan facilities rather than a single manufacturer reflects the vehicle's general-purpose nature. All Clans maintain Anhur fleets for logistics duties, though combat employment varies considerably by touman doctrine. Clans Blood Spirit, Hell's Horses, and Star Adder integrated the Anhur permanently into combat formations as an infantry assault transport, while Clans Fire Mandrill, Goliath Scorpion, Ice Hellion, and Snow Raven limited their use to ad hoc infantry transport when mission requirements demanded it.

The growing intensity of combat during the Jihad drove the development of the Anhur Transport BA, a dedicated infantry assault variant with an enlarged cargo bay, electronic countermeasures, and a revised armament suited for contested airspace. The Jihad also opened Inner Sphere production avenues: Gorton, Kingsley and Thorpe Enterprises on Rasalhague converted their line to produce the Anhur by 3068, extending the design's availability into the Inner Sphere Clan occupation zones. More unusual was the emergence of a heavily modified Anhur in Clan space circa 3074, operated by a Dark Caste raider band on Constance, demonstrating the Anhur's chassis could support significant reconfiguration far beyond its intended logistics role.

The Corax's chassis mounts a GM 210 XL engine on a UOC Light Spec 3 frame, giving the fighter an impressive thrust profile for its weight class. The use of an extralight engine frees up nine tons of pod space for weapons and equipment, though this comes at the cost of heat management, with only ten double heat sinks integrated into the base chassis. Outworld Weave Standard II armor provides adequate protection for a light fighter, while the Outworlds Advanced 6ai communications system and Multi-platform T12d targeting and tracking system handle sensor duties.

The Prime configuration mounts a large pulse laser in the nose supported by two wing-mounted medium lasers, providing considerable close-range firepower ideal for strafing runs, though the lack of any aft-facing weaponry leaves the fighter vulnerable when pursued. Alternative configurations address different tactical needs, with paired SRM-6 racks and rear-mounted small lasers for dogfighting, an all-energy loadout of medium pulse and standard medium lasers for extended operations, and even a ground suppression variant mounting a medium-range missile system sourced from the Draconis Combine.

The Corax is a thirty-ton Inner Sphere OmniFighter developed by the United Outworlders Corporation on Ramora for the Outworlds Alliance. Introduced in 3067, it holds the distinction of being the Alliance's first domestically produced OmniFighter, a feat that baffled military analysts across the Inner Sphere who questioned how a minor Periphery state could develop such advanced technology. Named in honor of the growing bond of friendship between the Outworlds Alliance and Clan Snow Raven, the Corax is a light, fast design intended primarily for defensive patrol and air superiority roles within Alliance space. Despite its modest size and limited pod capacity, the design earned a reputation as a capable light combatant that proved even Periphery nations could field competitive OmniFighter designs with the right partnerships.

The R configuration represents the deepest integration of Clan technology into the Corax platform. Three Clan-built ER medium lasers in the nose and Clan Streak SRM-4 launchers in each wing deliver exceptional firepower for a light fighter, all guided by an advanced targeting computer that dramatically improves accuracy. This mixed-technology loadout makes the R one of the most potent Corax configurations fielded by the Raven Alliance.

The Corax emerged from a partnership between the United Outworlders Corporation and Clan Snow Raven during the 3060s. The Snow Ravens had been cultivating a relationship with the Outworlds Alliance for years, and providing the technical expertise to develop an OmniFighter represented one of the most dramatic expressions of this growing bond. The exact nature and extent of the Clan's contribution remained deliberately obscure, with neither the Alliance nor the Draconis Combine willing to discuss the matter openly. Military intelligence agencies across the Inner Sphere scrambled to determine how a Periphery state had leaped ahead of several Great Houses in fielding an indigenous OmniFighter design, but the design showed little of the Combine influence common to other recent Periphery technological advances, and there seemed to be no other source for the Omni technology.

The entire first production run was assigned to the First Alliance Air Wing, replacing the Seydlitz conventional fighters that were redistributed to the Alliance's other four Air Wings. This concentration reflected both the First Wing's superior pilot skills and the practical reality that trained OmniFighter technicians were still in critically short supply across the Alliance.

The Word of Blake's Jihad struck the Ramora production facilities hard. Terrorist strikes by the Inferno organization destroyed worker habitats and damaged production lines, while a disinformation campaign tricked the Screaming Eagles mercenary unit into launching an attack on the world. A virulent strain of drug-resistant influenza also swept across Ramora, widely suspected to be another Blakist weapon. By 3079, the Ramora plant had lost half its workforce and was operating at only sixty percent of its pre-war capacity.

The formation of the Raven Alliance following the Snow Raven absorption of the Outworlds Alliance ensured the Corax's continued production under new political arrangements. United Outworlders Corporation, now operating under Raven Alliance oversight, maintained its position as the primary aerospace manufacturer in the former Alliance territories, with the Corax remaining a staple of the combined state's fighter wings.

The Goth mounts a Pitban 180 standard fusion engine on a Saroyan 2.5 CCC-OP airframe, producing a maximum thrust of eight Gs with a safe cruise of five. While not the fastest medium fighter, its acceleration is adequate for the interceptor role. The hull carries fourteen and a half tons of Forging OTR17b standard armor, providing respectable protection for sustained engagements against larger targets. Twenty-seven tons of available pod space give pilots considerable latitude in configuring the fighter for specific missions.

The design's primary weakness is heat management. Fifteen single heat sinks form the fixed cooling infrastructure, a system that struggles to keep pace with most weapon configurations. Nearly every loadout includes additional pod-mounted heat sinks to compensate. The Prime configuration pairs wing-mounted Artemis IV-guided LRM-15 launchers with coaxial small pulse lasers, supplemented by a nose-mounted large pulse laser and two ER medium lasers. Two additional ER medium lasers cover the rear arc. CCC T-55 communications and CCC D5.2J targeting systems round out the electronics package. The airframe's easy maintenance characteristics and integrated combat computer are offset by notable atmospheric flight instability, a quirk inherited from the original Gotha design.

The Goth is a sixty-ton Clan medium OmniFighter developed by Clan Cloud Cobra during the Golden Century. First entering service in 2873, the design was derived from the Inner Sphere Gotha aerospace fighter, transforming the proven airframe into a modular weapons platform through the application of OmniPod technology. Cloud Cobra engineers valued the Gotha's reputation for durability and ease of maintenance, qualities that translated well into the new configuration. Intended primarily as an anti-DropShip interceptor, the Goth filled a unique niche between the lighter Issus and the heavier Xerxes that no other Clan fighter occupied until the introduction of the Tyre in 2907. Its versatility and solid performance made the design popular across nearly every Clan, establishing it as one of the most widespread medium OmniFighters of its generation.

Another Wolf Empire configuration, the D variant combines an ER PPC fitted with a PPC capacitor in the nose with wing-mounted Artemis V-enhanced LRM-15 launchers supplied by six tons of ammunition. Five additional single heat sinks and two coolant pods help manage the severe thermal spikes generated by the capacitor-boosted particle cannon, giving this configuration both reach and devastating alpha-strike potential.

Clan Cloud Cobra developed the Goth in the years following the Political Century, seeking a dedicated anti-DropShip platform for their aerospace-heavy touman. The Cobras drew upon their extensive experience with the Gotha, an Inner Sphere design that had accompanied the Exodus fleet, recognizing that its robust airframe and maintainable systems provided an ideal foundation for OmniPod conversion. The resulting OmniFighter entered service in 2873 and quickly proved its worth in the Cloud Cobras' naval-centric doctrine.

The Goth spread rapidly through Trials of Possession and inter-Clan trade, becoming a common sight across Clan space within decades of its introduction. Typically deployed for space superiority and DropShip escort duties, the fighter saw some of its most notable action during Clan Coyote's punitive campaigns against Clan Cloud Cobra in 2948 and 2949. Flying as escorts for Hydaspeses class WarShips, Goths provided critical flexibility as zellbrigen broke down in the escalating conflict. The Cobras also tasked their Goths with hunting Coyote DropShips, a role in which the fighter proved devastatingly effective. Though the Cobras suffered heavy ground losses, the Coyotes' inability to resupply their forces contributed to their eventual withdrawal from the Cloud Cobra enclaves on Homer and Brim.

By the late 2900s, a new generation of faster OmniFighters began displacing the Goth from frontline service. The design was formally classified as obsolete around 2980, though many Clans retained it in second-line and garrison formations where its reliability and low maintenance requirements remained valuable assets.

The Goth experienced an unexpected revival in the ilClan era. After Stewart was absorbed into the Wolf Empire, Clan Wolf directed Allied Technologies to convert their existing Gotha production lines to manufacture the Goth beginning in 3146. This decision allowed the Wolves to rapidly bolster their depleted aerospace forces using established factory infrastructure. New Wolf Empire configurations mounting rotary autocannons and advanced missile systems demonstrated the continued viability of the venerable airframe with modern weaponry.
